# The Cult of Khaine

*Page PDF 119*

Knives of Khaine 

## **The Cult of Khaine**
Khaine is the god of murder, cruelty, and warfare. Just as the god has a thousand faces, every elf feels his pull in their own way. Energised by hatred and strife, Khaine has grown powerful. Most elves fear him more than even Asuryan, the cold king of the gods, but only the Druchii embrace his worship. 

## **Cult Hierarchy**
After the Sundering, the Cults of Slaanesh and Khaine vied for power amongst the Druchii. When Malerion declared himself Khaine’s vessel he made the cult the official religion of Naggaroth. The cult tried to destroy the cults of Slaanesh, backed by their king and their god. Today, they dominate Druchii society. Blood Queen Crone Hellebron, the greatest of the Brides of Khaine, is among Malerion’s closest advisors. 

The cult is matriarchal in its organisation. Beneath Hellebron are hag queens, spiritual leaders who preside over death hags, the high priestesses. Beneath them are Brides of Khaine, the warrior sisterhood of witch elves. Witch elf subcults have their own traditions, such as the Silent Sisters, who refuse to speak until the Widowmaker is drawn once again, or the Coven of Sorrows, who revere their god as Lord of Suffering. 

A parallel hierarchy administers the cult and collects tithes. The _Haru’ann_ are a council of six elders ruled by the grand carnifex, who answers to the hag queens. These acolytes, scholars, and temple servants are all proud murderers, but the witch elves disdain them as weak and impious. Many elders grow wealthy in their position and few venture far from the cities. 

The priesthood controls Har Ganeth through the Daughters of Despair, a ruling council of masked death hags, who order the city’s armies to do their bidding. The city guard have evolved into the Executioners, a legion of expert swordbearers under command of Tullaris Deathbringer. These slayers are respected and feared by all Druchii, as they are used to extend the reach of the cult and guard Khaine’s temples throughout Naggaroth and beyond. 

Infants stolen during Death Night are raised within the cult to become assassins, chosen killers for their god. These assassins are hired out by the cult in exchange for sacrifices, wealth, and political influence. While there is a master of assassins on the _Haru’ann_ council, they are effectively the property of the death hags. 

## **Death Night**
Centuries ago, Crone Hellebron broke a political stalemate in a single night by slaughtering hundreds of high-ranking elves loyal to Morathi. The malice behind these premeditated killings so impressed Malerion that, to win Hellebron to his side, he proclaimed the witch elves repeat the event once a year. 

On Death Night, witch elves roam the streets of Naggaroth in cackling gangs, butchering the foolish and unfortunate as they seek out targets they particularly despise. No one is truly safe on Death Night, and not all the slain are killed by Khaine’s brides. There is no easier time to get away with murder, as the witch elves might be responsible for almost anything. 

## **Worship**
True cultists feel an inexorable pull towards acts of malice: while some cultists raid and pillage across the world, others poison their neighbours. There is no wrong way to worship the god, providing death is involved. 

The cult depends on constant sacrifices in Naggaroth, exulting their god and demonstrating his dominion. These killings attract large gatherings everywhere from temples to public squares, where crowds grow raucous as blood rains upon them. The cruelty of these sacrifices hardens the masses through fear and the power of murder, pleasing Khaine. 

There are countless other rites to Khaine, which reflect different incarnations of the god or the cultural differences between cities and Druchii factions. In Clar Karond, the Rite of the Serpent Lord reveres Khaine in his aspect as an all-consuming snake, whereas Druchii in Ghrond pray to Khaine as the Iron Panther, stalker of the void.
